subject: general
question: Who introduced the Railways (Amendment) Bill that was passed in the Rajya Sabha in March 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashwini Vaishnaw**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ashwini Vaishnaw**, the current Union Minister for Railways, Communications, and Electronics & Information Technology, introduced the **Railways (Amendment) Bill** in the **Rajya Sabha** in **March 2025**.
 
• The bill aimed to bring comprehensive changes to the functioning and regulations of the Indian Railways, focusing on **modernization, safety, and efficiency**.
 
• This bill was part of the government's broader agenda to enhance **infrastructure development** and improve the operational framework of the railways in India.
 
• Ashwini Vaishnaw is known for his expertise in both administration and technology, which has significantly influenced reforms within the Indian Railways sector since his appointment in **July 2021**.
 
• His tenure has been marked by significant initiatives, including the introduction of **Vande Bharat trains** and the promotion of digitization within the railways.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Ashwini Vaishnaw:**

 
 
• He is a former IAS officer of the **1994 Odisha cadre** and holds an MBA from the **Wharton School**, University of Pennsylvania.
 
• Before entering politics, he worked in key roles in the **corporate sector** with companies such as **GE Transportation** and **Siemens**.
 
• He was appointed as the Minister of Railways, Communications, and Electronics & IT in **July 2021**, and since then, he has been instrumental in introducing reforms in these sectors.
 
 
 
• **Railways (Amendment) Bill 2025:**
 
 
• The bill introduced provisions to streamline the functioning of the Indian Railways, focusing on **public-private partnerships (PPP)** for infrastructure development.
 
• It emphasized **passenger safety**, **modernization of rail infrastructure**, and the reduction of operational inefficiencies.
 
• It also included proposals for the **introduction of green energy initiatives** in railway operations.
 
 
 
• **Indian Railways Modernization:**
 
 
• Indian Railways is the **fourth-largest railway network** in the world, operating over a vast network of **67,956 route kilometers**.
 
• Recent modernization efforts include the introduction of **semi-high-speed trains** like the **Vande Bharat Express** and electrification of railway tracks.
 
• Digitization initiatives, such as the **Rail Drishti Portal**, have been launched to improve transparency and passenger experience.
 
 
 
• **Other Ministers Mentioned:**
 
 
• **Kiren Rijiju:** Currently serves as the Minister of Earth Sciences and has held various positions in the Indian government but is not directly involved with the railways.
 
• **Sarbananda Sonowal:** Minister of Ports, Shipping, and Waterways, and Minister of AYUSH, focusing primarily on water-based transport and wellness initiatives.
 
• **Hardeep Singh Puri:** Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs and Petroleum & Natural Gas, contributing to urban development and energy sectors.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Indian Railways' Reforms:**

 
 
• Indian Railways is focusing on achieving **net-zero carbon emissions** by 2030 through electrification and renewable energy projects.
 
• Initiatives under the **National Rail Plan 2030** aim to increase the railways' share in freight transport to **45%**.
 
 
 
• **Role of Public-Private Partnerships:**
 
 
• The government is encouraging **PPP models** for the development of high-speed rail corridors, station modernization, and freight corridors.
 
• Examples include the **Ahmedabad-Mumbai Bullet Train Project**, India's first high-speed rail project.
